title: The summit: the circle begins again
hook: the Torah's end touches its beginning; the cycle begins again, with you in it
carry: who kept us alive for this
tomorrow: the scroll is open at the beginning again. what will you read first?

segments.voice: Last night, a king asking his children to stay one more day: the last night, slow and full. This morning, the top of the mountain.
screen: `THE LAST NIGHT.` → `THE TOP OF THE MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: First morning in a dorm room. Boxes everywhere, a bare mattress, a stranger's alarm through the wall. Noa's roommate, Layla, sits up, still half asleep, and says a few quiet words before her feet touch the floor. Later Noa asks what they were. Layla tells her: when the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, woke, he would praise God who gave us life again after sleep, and say that to him is the return. She has words for mornings like this one too. And on Simchat Torah, the scroll's last word comes and goes, and it rolls straight back to the first: Bereshit. In the beginning.
screen: `BOXES, A BARE MATTRESS.` → `LAYLA'S MORNING WORDS.` → `BERESHIT: IN THE BEGINNING.`

segments.voice: Here's the question at the summit: what do you say when you've arrived? On Simchat Torah, Deuteronomy ends with Moses, and in the same breath someone reads, in the JPS translation: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." No gap. Some readers notice the Torah's last letter, the lamed of Israel, and its first, the bet of Bereshit. Together they spell lev: heart. The circle closes on a heart and opens again. And for arriving, the Mishnah gives a blessing. Someone who builds a new house or gets new things says it, and it's also said at the start of festivals and at other firsts: blessed are you, Lord our God, ruler of the universe, who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time. Shehecheyanu. Now the shared ground, in Layla's own tradition's words. The hadith collection of al-Bukhari records the Prophet's waking words: praise to God who gave us life after death, the death of sleep, and to him is the return. Both give thanks for simply being alive to meet this moment. And the honest difference: Layla's words greet every ordinary morning, and hear sleep as a small death and waking as life given back. Shehecheyanu waits for the new and the rare: a first, a season, a summit, and thanks God for bringing you to it. Neither needs the other to be smaller.
screen: `THE END ROLLS BACK TO THE START.` · `LAMED AND BET: A HEART.` · `SHEHECHEYANU: BROUGHT US TO THIS.` · `LAYLA'S WORDS: LIFE AGAIN, EACH DAY.` · then, large: `WHO KEPT US ALIVE FOR THIS.`

segments.voice: Think of one first in your life right now: a new place, a new season, a summit like this one. If you pray, you can say the blessing out loud, in Hebrew or in English: who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time. If not, simply name the first out loud, and let yourself be glad you're here for it.
screen: `ONE FIRST, RIGHT NOW.` · `THE BLESSING, IF YOU PRAY.` · `OR NAME IT, AND BE GLAD.`

segments.voice: Shehecheyanu: who has kept us alive. The blessing for firsts, seasons and arrivals, and the last word of these five years.
The summit's line: who kept us alive for this, from Nebo to now. Fourteen of fourteen, and back to the beginning.

howItsDone: Jews say the Shehecheyanu blessing for firsts: new fruit, new clothes or a new home, the first night of a festival, a milestone. On Simchat Torah the last verses of Deuteronomy are read and the reading starts again at Genesis 1.

Shehecheyanu.meaning: the blessing 'who has kept us alive', said for firsts

Simchat Torah.meaning: the festival when the Torah reading ends and begins again

Bereshit.meaning: in the beginning; the Torah's first word

hadith.meaning: a recorded saying or action of the Prophet Muhammad

sources.quoted: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth

sources.ref: Mishnah Berakhot 9:3 (one who builds a new house or buys new vessels says: blessed is he who has kept us alive, sustained us and brought us to this time)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6312 (the Prophet's words on waking: praise to God who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the return)
Deuteronomy 34:12 (last word, Israel) and Genesis 1:1 (first word, Bereshit)

notes: Unity thread (wisdom day): shared ground with Islam (Noa's roommate Layla), in Islam's own source (Sahih al-Bukhari 6312, paraphrased, with 'peace be upon him' at first mention of the Prophet); one honest difference (every morning vs firsts and seasons). The lamed + bet = lev observation is framed as 'some readers notice'; it is checkable in the Hebrew text (ישראל / בראשית).
